sources.entry: OpenClaw — Open-source personal AI assistant / agent framework

summary.name: OpenClaw
summary.one_liner: OpenClaw is an open-source personal AI assistant that runs on your own machine and acts on your behalf (email, calendar, files, web) through chat apps like WhatsApp and Telegram.
keywords: run ai on my own computer
use_cases: Organizing an inbox and sending emails from a chat app
Managing a calendar and checking in for flights
Running scheduled reminders, cron jobs and daily briefings
Sharing one assistant gateway with a small team
Automating browser forms, file edits and shell commands on your own machine
Building and extending personal agent skills and plugins
summary.what_it_does: The page describes OpenClaw as software that runs on macOS, Linux or Windows and keeps its state on your machine, with models that can be hosted, subscription-backed, gateway or local. You talk to it over WhatsApp, Telegram, Discord, Slack, Signal, iMessage or any of its 29 listed channels, in DMs or group chats. It is said to remember preferences, projects and people across conversations. It can browse the web, fill forms, read and write files and run shell commands, with either full access or a sandbox. Extensions come from community skills and plugins, which it can also write itself.
notable: Stewarded by an independent US 501(c)(3) nonprofit foundation; MIT licensed with no enterprise or paid edition
Runs natively on Windows inside Microsoft Execution Containers, per the page
Native iOS and Android apps paired to your own Gateway
Works with 29 chat channels and supports team-shared gateways
caveats: Full system access (shell, files, browser) carries risk unless sandboxed, which the page describes as an option
Some models may require the user's own subscriptions or API access (hosted, subscription-backed or local models are all listed as options)
Default install sends a daily version check to the Foundation; this can be turned off
